definition: The query language of Log Analytics, Application Insights, Sentinel and Azure Data Explorer. A query starts with a table and pipes rows through steps such as where, summarize, project, join and render. It maps closely onto T-SQL; always filter on time first.
example: AppRequests | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) and Success == false | summarize count() by Name

definition: The pricing and capability tier of each table in a Log Analytics workspace. Analytics is full price with fast queries and alerting; Basic costs roughly a quarter plus a charge per GB scanned and cannot drive alerts; Auxiliary is cheapest, for verbose logs searched rarely.
example: Front Door access logs move to Basic while WAF logs, which are alerted on, stay on Analytics.

definition: How long a workspace keeps each table's data. Analytics tables include 31 days at no extra charge and can be retained interactively for up to two years; long-term retention keeps data for up to 12 years at a fraction of the price, searched or restored when needed. Match it to audit and investigation needs.
example: Key Vault audit events are interactive for 90 days and kept for a year in long-term retention.

definition: A Log Analytics pricing option that discounts ingestion in exchange for committing to a daily volume, starting at 100 GB a day. Worth it only when volume is steady and predictable; below the commitment you still pay for the full tier.
example: A large estate ingesting a steady 300 GB a day saves by moving from pay-as-you-go to a 300 GB commitment tier.

definition: An interactive report in Azure Monitor built from KQL queries, metrics and parameters - charts, grids and links in one page. Workbooks can be saved as templates and deployed with the infrastructure, so every environment has the same view.
example: The Shop health workbook shows error rate, p95 latency, queue depth, WAF blocks and ingestion by table.
